newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian seismic oil exploration hits record.
newsitem.headline: Australian seismic oil exploration hits record.

text.p: The Australian oil exploration industry conducted a record volume of seismic surveying last year, foreshadowing an imminent boost in drilling, the Bureau of Resource Sciences said on Tuesday.
"During 1996 more than 390,000 line-kilometres of seismic data were recorded, over a third more than (the previous) year," the bureau said in a statement.
"Offshore, over 328,000 line-kilometres of high-quality 3D seismic data were collected, which is the highest level of 3D seismic data ever collected."
Seismic surveys are a preliminary search for oil. Geologists set off explosives on the surface and then listen for the echo, which reveals the types and formations of the rock below.
The explosions are set off in lines and several lines set off at once can produce a three-dimensional picture of the rock.
Promising results encourage oil companies to drill, and the bureau said last year's volume of seismic survey suggested more drilling to come.
"Seismic survey data acquisition normally precedes drilling operations and high levels are likely to lead to increased levels of drilling activity," it said.
Offshore exploration drilling had declined to 47 wells in 1996 from 56 in 1995, a near-record year, the bureau said.
"Exploration drilling this year (1996) has led to several oil and gas discoveries in the Timor Sea area and in the offshore Canarvon Basin," it said.
Onshore exploration drilling had risen, however, to 96 wells from 92 previously.
